summary: Full-stack validation of MediStock Pro. Backend: 60-test pytest suite (auth/RBAC, dashboard, reports, products, inventory, POS sales incl. FEFO/idempotency/expired-batch, returns, purchases + CSV import, ledgers/payments, expenses, settings/staff) — 58 passed, 2 failed (genuine business-logic bugs in sales returns), 3 skipped (expired-batch fixtures consumed during UI testing; they passed on the first run). Frontend: end-to-end Playwright runs across Login, Dashboard KPIs+charts, POS cash sale (invoice INV-2026-27-000006 with CGST/SGST), POS credit sale (Udhar outstanding rose to Rs.31), Inventory (batch expand, stock adjust 37->36, Reorder tab), Products (add + edit), Purchases (new purchase PUR-xxxx -> batch UIB101 visible in Inventory) and CSV Import (Load sample -> preview Total 2/Matched 1/New 1/Errors 0 -> commit 'Imported 2 items'), Sales & Returns (invoice view, SR-xxxx return + tabs), Expiry (all 5 buckets, purchase-return of expired batch), Customers (add, ledger, payment 31->26), Suppliers (add, payment), Udhar Khata (collect), Expenses (777 added), Reports (Sales/GST-HSN/Stock Valuation + CSV downloads), Settings (profile save, staff add, audit log), RBAC cashier sidebar, plus mobile 390px layout (no overflow, bottom nav filtered).

critical.issue: Cumulative returned qty is not tracked. Validation only compares the requested qty against the original sale-item qty, so the SAME sale item can be fully returned repeatedly - each time restocking the batch and refunding again (reproduced: 2 units sold, returned 2 twice, second call returned 200 with refund Rs.235.2). Fix: sum existing sales_return items for the sale_item_id and reject qty > (sold - already_returned).

Cancel does not account for prior returns and does not block cancelling a returned/partially-returned sale, so stock is restored twice (reproduced: batch 15 -> 17 after full return + cancel). Also allows cancel after refund was already issued. Fix: block cancel when returns exist (or subtract returned qty) and mark cancelled sales non-returnable.

minor.issue: Does not validate that the batch was actually purchased from the selected supplier - any batch can be returned to any supplier, creating an incorrect supplier debit.

Not gated by require_module - a cashier (no 'customers' write intent beyond udhar) or any authenticated staff can post customer AND supplier payments; supplier payments should require the 'suppliers' module.
Only require authentication (no module gate). Acceptable for POS, but it means a cashier can enumerate the full product/supplier master; confirm this is intended.

ui_bugs.issue: No permission-based route guard. Logged in as cashier@medistock.demo, navigating directly to /purchases, /products, /inventory, /settings renders the full restricted page (New Purchase form with Save Purchase, CSV Import, Business Profile/Staff tabs). Only the sidebar/bottom-nav is filtered. Guard routes with the permissions from /api/auth/me and redirect to /.

ui_bugs.component: Inventory.jsx / Dashboard.jsx / Reports.jsx / Purchases.jsx / Sales.jsx / Expiry.jsx / POS.jsx
ui_bugs.issue: ~14 api.get() calls have no .catch() handler. As cashier on /inventory this produced a CRA 'Uncaught runtime errors: Request failed with status code 403' full-screen overlay plus a permanent loading spinner. Every fetch needs loading/error state.

No blocking contrast/spacing/alignment problems found on desktop 1920x1080 or mobile 390x844; no horizontal overflow; sidebar, KPI cards, tables and dialogs render correctly

action_items: CRITICAL: track cumulative returned qty in POST /api/sales-returns so a sale item cannot be returned more than it was sold (currently unlimited refunds + stock inflation).
HIGH: make POST /api/sales/{id}/cancel return-aware - reject cancel when returns exist and reject returns on cancelled sales.
HIGH: add permission-based route guarding in App.js/Protected so restricted pages are not renderable by roles lacking the module (cashier currently sees /purchases, /products, /inventory, /settings).
HIGH: add .catch()/error state to all api.get() calls (Inventory, Dashboard, Reports, Purchases, Sales, Expiry, POS) - a 403/500 currently crashes the page with a runtime-error overlay.
MINOR: validate batch-supplier relationship in POST /api/purchase-returns; gate POST /api/payments by module (supplier payments) as appropriate.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1461 lines - split into routers (sales, purchases, inventory, parties, reports, settings) for maintainability.

Stock mutations use read-then-$inc without a guard on available_qty; under concurrency (two POS terminals) a batch can go negative. Use a conditional update ({'available_qty': {'$gte': qty}}) and check modified_count.
Sales/purchase writes are multi-document without transactions; a mid-flow failure leaves partial stock/ledger state. Consider Mongo transactions or compensating logic.
Money is stored as floats; ledger balances already show accumulated rounding risk - consider integer paise or Decimal128 for financial fields.
Owner bcrypt hash verified as $2b$ format; JWT auth, 401/403 handling and _id exclusion are correct across all tested endpoints.

success_rate.frontend: 94% (all 15 UI flows functional; 2 HIGH defects: missing route guard + unhandled API error overlay)

The 2 remaining failures (test_repeated_returns_cannot_exceed_sold_qty, test_cancel_after_return_should_not_double_restock) are the real bugs to re-verify after the fix. 3 tests skip because the seeded EXPIRED batch was consumed by my UI purchase-return test; to re-test 'expired batch cannot be sold' / purchase-return-of-expired, insert a batch with a past expiry_date directly in Mongo (seed is idempotent and will not recreate it). rca_of_the_issue: sales-returns validation compares only the incoming qty against the original sale-item qty and never aggregates previously returned quantities; likewise /sales/{id}/cancel blindly re-adds every sale item's qty regardless of returns/status. Both paths therefore inflate batch available_qty and issue duplicate refunds. On the frontend, App.js Protected only checks user+business (not the permissions array from /api/auth/me), so restricted pages mount for any role and their unguarded api.get() promises reject with 403, surfacing a CRA runtime-error overlay.
